title: Email server outage
matches: Can't access Exchange server, is it down?
symptoms: Several users at once cannot send or receive mail, or one site cannot reach its mail server. Users ask whether the email or Exchange server is down.
cause: The Exchange or regional mail server is down or unreachable: a stopped transport service, a failed node, an expired certificate, or a network path to one site's server.
resolution: Check the mail server's health in monitoring and test sending from Outlook on the web to tell a server fault from a client fault.
If the server is down, raise or link to one P1 major incident and post a status notice.
Restart the stopped Exchange transport services, or fail over to the standby node.
If only one site (for example Oregon) is affected, check the network route and DNS record for that site's mail server.
Link every user report to the major incident as a child instead of working them separately.
notes: This keeps coming back (INC0000032 says "down again"). After restoring service, open a problem record to find the root cause.

title: Email slow, not loading or can't connect
matches: Email is slow when an attachment is involved
symptoms: One user's Outlook can't connect, won't open messages, or is very slow, often when sending or opening attachments. Other users are fine.
cause: Usually a local problem: a corrupted Outlook cache (OST) or profile, a mailbox near its size limit, a slow network link, or an add-in scanning attachments.
resolution: Check Outlook on the web. If mail works there, the server is fine and the problem is the client.
Check mailbox size against the quota and archive or clean up if it is near the limit.
Close Outlook, rename the .ost file in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Outlook`, and reopen Outlook to rebuild the cache.
Start Outlook with `outlook.exe /safe`. If it is fast, disable add-ins one at a time to find the slow one.
If it still fails, create a new Outlook profile from Control Panel > Mail.
notes: If several users report the same thing at once, treat it as a server outage (KB0010001).

title: Password reset and sign-in problems
matches: Cannot sign into the company portal app
symptoms: User forgot their password, is locked out, or can't sign in to an app or the company portal.
cause: Forgotten or expired password, an account locked after too many attempts, or old saved credentials after a password change.
resolution: Verify the user's identity using the standard check (employee ID and manager, or a call-back).
Unlock the account and set a temporary password that must be changed at next sign-in, or point the user to self-service password reset.
Ask the user to clear saved passwords for the app (Windows Credential Manager, browser, phone mail app).
Have the user sign in once while you're on the call to confirm it works.
notes: Encourage self-service reset to cut these tickets. Repeated lockouts can mean an old device is still using the old password.

title: Business application outage (SAP, payroll)
symptoms: Users can't reach an SAP module (Sales, Materials Management, HR, Financial Accounting, Controlling) or the payroll application, or it is very slow. Often several modules at once.
cause: A shared back end is down or overloaded: the SAP application or database server, the message server or login service, or the payroll app server. Several SAP modules failing together points to a shared component.
resolution: Check whether one module or several are affected. Several at once means a shared back-end problem, so raise one P1 major incident.
Check the application and database servers in monitoring (CPU, memory, disk, services).
For SAP, check the message server and work processes, and restart failed instances in the documented order.
For payroll, restart the application service, then the integration service, and tell HR leadership if pay deadlines are at risk.
If only one user can't log in (for example from their laptop), check their SAP GUI connection settings and account lock instead.
notes: Four SAP tickets (Sales, HR, Financial Accounting, Controlling) came in on Sep 20, 2026, within hours of each other. Link them to one parent incident.

title: Shared drive and file share access
matches: Unable to access the shared folder
Need access to the common drive
symptoms: User can't open a shared folder, team share or home directory, gets access denied, or the network drive is missing or unavailable.
cause: Either the user isn't in the security group for that share, the drive mapping is missing, or the file server or network storage is down.
resolution: Ask for the exact path (for example `\\server\share`) and the error message.
If several users can't reach the same share, check the file server or NAS in monitoring and treat it as an outage.
If one user gets access denied, check the share's security group. Add them only with the data owner's approval.
If the drive or home directory is missing, remap it or run `gpupdate /force` and sign out and back in.
Confirm the user can open and save a file.
notes: A request for new access (like INC0007002) should go through the access request catalog item, not an incident.

title: File is read-only or locked, and folder how-to
matches: PDF docs are all locked from editing
How do I create a sub-folder
symptoms: User can open a file but can't edit or save it, or needs help with basic file tasks like creating a folder.
cause: Someone else has the file open, a stale lock file was left behind, the file is marked read-only or protected, or the user only has read permission on the folder.
resolution: Check whether someone else has the file open (Excel shows who). Ask them to close it.
Look for a hidden lock file (`~$filename`) in the same folder and delete it if nobody has the file open.
Check file properties: untick Read-only, and for PDFs check whether the document has an editing password.
Check folder permissions. If the user needs write access, get the data owner's approval.
For how-to questions, walk the user through it and send the self-help article.
notes: How-to questions are not incidents. Close them as requests with a link to the article.

title: Server health: storage full, backup failed, CPU, data center
matches: Backup did not occur last night
CPU load high for over 10 minutes
Rain is leaking on main DNS server
symptoms: A monitoring alert or engineer reports a server problem: disk filling up, a missed backup, sustained high CPU, or physical risk to equipment.
cause: Capacity not planned for growth, a failed or skipped backup job, a runaway process, or a facilities problem in the server room.
resolution: Physical risk (water, heat, power) comes first: protect or power down the equipment safely and call facilities.
Disk full: find large or old files, clear temp and logs, and raise a change to add storage before it reaches 90%.
Missed backup: check the backup console for the job's error, rerun it, and confirm it completes.
High CPU: find the process in Task Manager or `top`, restart it if it's hung, and check for a recent change.
Record the root cause and add a monitoring threshold so it's caught earlier.
notes: INC0000016 (water on the DNS server) threatens a core service. Treat it as P1 and have a DNS failover plan ready.

title: Wi-Fi, network and VPN connectivity
matches: Wireless access is down in my area
Lost connection to the wireless network
Can't launch VPN client since the last software update
symptoms: User loses Wi-Fi, has slow wireless, has a general network problem, or the VPN client won't start.
cause: A failed or overloaded wireless access point, an expired Wi-Fi certificate, a bad adapter driver, or a software update that broke the VPN client.
resolution: Ask where the user is. If several users in one area have no Wi-Fi, check that area's access point and controller.
For one user, forget and rejoin the network, and update the wireless adapter driver.
Test speed on wired and wireless to tell a Wi-Fi problem from a wider network problem.
If the VPN client won't launch after an update, reinstall the approved VPN version from Software Center, or roll back the update.
Confirm the user can reach an internal site.
notes: Escalate to Network with the location, access point name and time if a whole area is affected.

title: PC hardware faults (disk, USB, audio, memory)
matches: The USB port on my PC stopped working
Computer is not detecting the headphone device
Need to add more memory to laptop
symptoms: A part of the user's computer fails: a USB port, headphones not detected, disk errors or files that can't be deleted, or not enough memory.
cause: Failing hardware, a missing or bad driver, or a machine below the current specification.
resolution: Restart the computer and check Device Manager for errors on the device.
Reinstall or update the driver (audio, USB, chipset) from the manufacturer or Software Center.
For disk problems, run `chkdsk /f` and check the drive's health (SMART). Back up the user's data first if it's failing.
For memory, check the model's maximum and order the upgrade, or swap the laptop if it is below spec.
If a part has failed, log a hardware repair or replacement with the asset tag.
notes: A failing disk is urgent. Back up first, then repair.

title: Printing and fax problems
matches: Printer in my office is out of toner
Hangs when trying to print VISIO document
symptoms: Printer out of toner, the app hangs when printing one kind of document, or a fax didn't arrive.
cause: Consumables run out, a stuck print queue or bad printer driver, or a failed fax job or wrong number.
resolution: Toner or paper: send a supply order or replace the cartridge, and check the printer's status page.
App hangs when printing: clear the print queue, restart the Print Spooler service, and update the printer driver.
Try printing the same file to PDF. If that works, the problem is the printer driver.
Fax not received: check the fax server's log for the job, confirm the number, and resend.
notes: Toner requests should go through the supplies catalog item, not an incident.

title: Software install, patch and virtual machine problems
matches: Please remove the latest hotfix from my PC
symptoms: User needs software installed or a patch removed, or a virtual machine won't start.
cause: A hotfix that broke something, software that isn't in the self-service catalog, or virtualization turned off in BIOS or not supported by the host.
resolution: Hotfix: confirm which update caused the problem, uninstall it from Settings > Windows Update > Update history, and pause it until it's fixed.
Install requests: check the license and approval, then install from Software Center or package it.
64-bit VM won't start: turn on Intel VT-x or AMD-V in BIOS, and turn off Hyper-V if the VM software needs it.
Confirm the user's software now works.
notes: Report a bad hotfix to the patching team so it can be stopped for everyone.

title: Business app access and slowness (Sales, SFA, payroll portal)
matches: Unable to access the personal details section in payroll portal
symptoms: One user can't get into a business app or one part of it, or the app is slow for them.
cause: Missing role or license, a page the user's role doesn't allow, or performance problems on the app or its database.
resolution: Ask for the exact app, page and error message.
Check the user's roles and license in the app. Missing access goes to the access request process with manager approval.
If it's slow, check whether others see it too. If yes, check the app and database servers. If no, check the user's network and browser.
Confirm the user can reach the page they need.
notes: If the whole app is down for everyone, use KB0010004.

title: Internal websites, wiki and IT tools
matches: Unable to post content on a Wiki page
Issue with a web page on wiki
JavaScript error on hiring page of corporate website
symptoms: An internal site, wiki page, corporate web page or IT tool shows errors, won't load, or can't be changed.
cause: A recent site change, a page script error, missing edit permission, or the tool's server being down.
resolution: Ask for the page link, a screenshot and the browser.
Try it in a private window to rule out the browser cache and extensions.
For a script error, open the browser console (F12), note the error and pass it to the site owner.
For wiki editing, check the user's edit permission on that space.
If a tool is down for everyone, check its server and raise an outage.
notes: Configuration requests (such as changing a tool's UI) are changes, not incidents.

title: Phones and mobile devices
matches: My desk phone does not work
symptoms: Desk phone is dead or has no dial tone, or a user needs a mobile phone replaced or set up.
cause: Loose cable or failed PoE port, a phone not registered with the phone system, or a damaged or new mobile device.
resolution: Desk phone: check the network cable and power, try another port, and check the phone's registration.
Replacement phone: confirm eligibility, order from the mobile catalog, and transfer the number.
New mobile setup: enroll it in device management, then set up email and apps.
notes: Device orders are requests. Only a broken device is an incident.

title: Service requests logged as incidents
symptoms: The ticket asks for something new (a service, onboarding a new hire) rather than reporting something broken.
cause: The user picked the wrong form, or the request catalog item isn't easy to find.
resolution: Thank the user and open the right request (for example New Hire Onboarding) with their details.
Link the request to the incident and close the incident as "Logged as request".
Send the user the link to the catalog item for next time.
notes: Many of these mean the catalog needs a clearer entry point.

title: ATF test records
symptoms: Tickets named "ATF" or "Test" that no user reported.
cause: Created by the ServiceNow Automated Test Framework (ATF) or by someone testing the instance.
resolution: Confirm with the platform team that the test run has finished.
Close the records as "Test" or delete them on a test instance.
Have ATF clean up the records it creates so they don't appear in reports.
notes: These tickets distort counts. Leave them out of reporting.
